r.정치 구도: A parliamentary system led by the prime minister, with 28 powerful states that are sometimes governed by different parties. The Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has led the central government since 2014; in the 2024 election it lost its single-party majority and formed a government with coalition partners. With more than 900 million voters, general elections take several weeks. Caste-based quotas, religious tension and the interests of states with different languages are major forces in politics.

t.why: The world's most populous country and a large, fast-growing economy. It forms the Quad security dialogue with the United States, Japan and Australia while buying arms and oil from Russia and belonging to BRICS and the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, a foreign policy it calls 'strategic autonomy'. It presents itself as a voice for the developing 'Global South' and has long sought a permanent seat on the UN Security Council. It has border disputes with both Pakistan and China, and all three have nuclear weapons. Jutting into the middle of the Indian Ocean, it overlooks the sea route bringing Middle East oil to Asia.
t.rel: It has fought several wars with Pakistan over Kashmir, with another armed clash in 2025. It has a Himalayan border dispute with China and pursues 'strategic autonomy', siding fully with neither the United States nor Russia.
t.korea: The two established relations in 1973, and their Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement took effect in 2010. Hyundai, Samsung and LG run big factories there, and with its population still growing it is one of the markets Korean companies are most hopeful about. In reshaping supply chains to reduce reliance on China, Korea and India see each other as important alternatives. In defense, the K9 self-propelled howitzer has been co-produced in India. The tale of King Kim Suro of Gaya and the Indian princess Heo Hwang-ok is often cited as a sign of the two countries' ancient ties.
t.know: India makes more films than any other country: well over 1,000 a year in many languages.
etext: Its population is the world's largest and fairly young. With many English-speaking tech workers, it handles more software development, call centers and support work for multinationals than any other country.
It makes generic drugs cheaply and in bulk, earning the name 'pharmacy of the world'. Its vaccine production is among the largest in the world.
Subsidies to attract factories have rapidly increased assembly of Apple's iPhones. Companies looking for the next production base after China are watching.
Many people still depend on farming, and good jobs are scarce. Roads, power and regulatory procedures are a burden for investors.
